claim: Lab saves go to JSON files under src/content/scene/stages and src/content/scene/characters; neither directory exists and nothing loads from them, so runtime content comes only from the TS constants and every stage-lab save is a dead write (split-brain).

The determinism guard is two regexes/selectors that only match the literal call shapes Math.random(), Date.now(), performance.now(), new Date(); aliasing, destructuring, Math.random.call, crypto.getRandomValues/randomUUID, Date() and Math?.random?.() pass both, and application (which will host tick) has no determinism rule at all.

The layer test is a regex import scanner that cannot see require(), import x = require(), template-literal or variable dynamic import(), or node: built-ins in domain/application, and it does not enforce the content/scene -> interfaces/three-only rule or detect cycles.

Epoch-agnosticism of domain/application is guarded by a hand-typed denylist of 5 Highglass ids (plus a PlaySession-only string check); the second content pack is unguarded, and no check forbids any content-id-shaped literal in domain/application.

The accepted core-model and hardening invariants have no automated guard and the codebase already shows the drift they would catch: id-order is sorted at some sites and not at others, and slices accept Map/Set silently.

Adding one character or prop touches 3 hand-synced files joined by bare string ids, and only two of the joins are checked by one pack-specific test, not by any load-time validator; stage props are never checked against the pack.

The registry is a closed 11-kind class: adding a kind means editing the Zod file, EpochModulePackInput, a Map field, a snapshot and a restore line in registerPack, a registerX, a getX and the domain barrel, and the accepted-core-model kinds (thread runtime, resource ledger profile, instrument profiles, presence tables, tellProfile, CharacterBible, pools) would make it a god-registry. | Several registry checks are inconsistent or redundant: assertSeparationWeight re-implements a Zod bound, while OfficeBlueprint.institutionalLineageId, which is the same kind of reference as the checked thread lineage ids, is never validated; 7 of 8 typed getters have no non-test caller.

verify is 5.3-6.7 s wall because five steps run sequentially as five nested npm processes with two separate vitest startups; running them in parallel measured 2.4 s and merging the vitest runs saves ~0.5 s, with nothing weakened.

Part of the architecture suite guards prose rather than behaviour: it pins literal sentences and model names inside two SKILL.md files and the exact lint-staged array, so editing a skill or hook fails verify while protecting no engine property, and the real hook never runs verify.

ESLint runs only untyped configs (tseslint.configs.strict, no projectService), so no-floating-promises and switch-exhaustiveness-check cannot fire; a floating promise and a non-exhaustive switch both lint clean.
